imperial_sardukar: Imperial Sardukar The Imperial Sardukar was created by the [[aragorn|Emperor]] . It is commanded by [[ser_barristan-the_bold|Ser Barristan the Bold]] . It is a [[imperial_officeholders_and_appointees#household_troops|Imperial Household Military Unit]] . The Imperial Sardukar consists of specially trained shock troops and knights who have embraced a code that allows them to deal with a greater variety of situations and opponents.  In addition to its Hoplite style infantry sections, it includes a Heavy Cavalry century that rides with the Emperor in war or diplomacy, or for functions of state. Official Charter - raw
imperial_think_tank: Imperial Think Tank In large part because of [[mica|Mica "Wiley" of the Nine]] , the [[start|The Free Imperia]] has way more than its share of geniuses.  The R&D department of the [[field_engineering_corps|Field Engineering Corps]] is tasked with maintaining a conversation area with every creature comfort, good conversation, and open blackboards, as well as actively inviting superior intellects to participate and making them welcome.  The administrators delight in finding out what the favorite snacks and beverages are of talents they want to attract. For promising ideas, they also make engineers available, and work with other organizations including the [[order_magika_mage_college|Order Magika]] , [[church_of_eru|Church of Eru Ilùvatar]] , the [[tinker_gnomes|Tinker Gnomes]] , and the [[alchemists|Alchemists]] to provide skills they don't possess.
imperial_timber_operation:
Imperial Timber Operation Timber is ecologically harvested around the [[gulf_of_the_firstborn|Gulf of the Firstborn]] , in the far Northeast of Endórë, and seasoned and pre-worked at [[in39|Imperial Navy Fort IN#39]] before being gathered into Southbound fleets. Some gather at [[in38|Imperial Navy Fort IN#38]] ,  sometimes picking up extra escorts at [[in37|Imperial Navy Fort IN#37]] , along with merchant ships carrying furs and amber, the timber fleets proceed Southward along Endórë's East Coast to the [[great_silvanesti_bay|Great Sylvanesti Bay]] . Increasing numbers of timber fleets instead gather at the Westernmost embayment of the [[gulf_of_the_firstborn|Gulf of the Firstborn]] , and travel via Skylock to [[smash|Thane Smash]] 's Faerun Dwarfhold of [[argentum_capita|Argentum Capita]] ,
 joining the [[inland_waterway|Great Inland Waterway]] at its Northern end.  They proceed in fleets down the [[silver_river|Silver River]] to the [[white_eagle_kagonesti_tribe|White Eagle Kagonesti Tribe]] 's nominal Capital of [[wild_mountains|Wild Mountains]] on the [[kagonesti_basin|Kagonesti Basin]] . From here, whichever southing the timber fleets took, they proceed via the [[inland_waterway|Inland Waterway]] at [[semboch|Semboch]] or [[new_silvan|New Silvan]] , onwards to [[nexus_prime:start|Nexus Prime]] .
in1: Imperial Navy Fort IN#1 Map: N21 The first construction on [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] was the double Island Fortress of Imperial Navy Ouptost #1 in the mouth of the Orróduinë, or [[east_river|East River]] .  Working with the natural estuaries, the center two islands were fortified and joined by a drawbridge so high that it doesn't need lifted to allow ships to sail the center channel; it is only moved to separate the forts. The forts are joined to the shore with drawbridges, which if lifted allow passage in the outer channels as well. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in2: Imperial Navy Ouptost IN#2 The Olyas Yard Map: O20 The second Naval Outpost was built along the banks at the mouth of the [[great_southern_river|Great Southern River]] (Q. Harduinë ), where it enters the [[firth_of_olyas|Firth of Olyas]] .  The Eastern anchorage is further protected by a breakwall.  Wet Navy and Spelljammer repairs and provisioning are readily available, though there is no construction of large hulls. In the Second Age, this was the capital city of the rebellious son of the Fifth Nazgûl, which he called Kadar Abar-narîk (Ad. “Citadel of Iron Eagles”). He raised great support here, both among the Numenoreans and the native folk to resist his father's evil rule to the West. Apart from a tantalizing reference in a children's skipping rhyme about driving the Storm King away, and barring a few ancient granite blocks serving as foundations for shepherds' huts, it is hard to tell the Numenoreans were ever here, and certainly the native  population seems oblivious to their ancient history. Most of them have been friendly, and they seem largely undisturbed by elves and magic.  They herd cattle, sheep, and horses, and grow excellent pears and cherries from which they distill smoothly potent brandies. The outer points of the channel mouth are guarded by two more [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] forts, [[in5|IN#5]] on the West, and [[in6|IN#6]] to the East on [[imperial_point|Imperial Point]] , the forested point of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] which separates the [[firth_of_olyas|Firth of Olyas]] from the [[jojojopo_forest_bay|Jojojopo Forest Bay]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in3: Imperial Navy Fort IN#3 Map: N22 Naval Outposts IN#3 and [[in4|IN#4]] are the forts on the points that control the harbor mouth leading into [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] from the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] .  In addition to significant artillery batteries, they are the bases for dedicated harbor patrol vessels, both of the fast interceptor variety and mobile artillery platforms. IN#3 is the larger fort on the Southern point of the Harbor mouth. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in4: Imperial Navy Fort IN#4 Map: N22 Naval Outposts [[in3|IN#3]] and IN#4 are the forts on the points that control the harbor mouth leading into [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] from the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] .  In addition to significant artillery batteries, they are the bases for dedicated harbor patrol vessels, both of the fast interceptor variety and mobile artillery platforms. IN#4 is the smaller fort on the Northern point of the Harbor mouth, and has significant landward defenses. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in5: Imperial Navy Fort IN#5 Map: P20 Fortified lighthouse on the SW Point of the [[firth_of_olyas|Firth of Olyas]] leading to the mouth of the [[great_southern_river|Great Southern River]] and the [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] Fortifications of [[in2|IN#2]] .  Two minor harbors are protected by breakwalls, housing the Firth's protective squadron.  The only nightlife is of the rougher sort, in the Olyas Kriis hill villages nearby. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in6: Imperial Navy Fort IN#6 Map: P21 Fortified lighthouse on [[imperial_point|Imperial Point]] , the point of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] which divides the [[firth_of_olyas|Firth of Olyas]] from the wilderness of [[jojojopo_forest_bay|Jojojopo Forest Bay]] .  A breakwall helps shelter a wide harbor that houses the Bay Squadron, which protects the [[jojojopo_forest_bay|Jojojopo Forest Bay]] and reinforces the Firth Squadron at need.  Often partly garrisoned by Krynnic Elves who live throughout the adjoining forest. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in7: Imperial Navy Fort IN#7 Anchoring the Western end of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] on the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] side, IN#7 is a serious fortification from the land and water approaches, with plenty of heavy artillery and a strong garrison and squadron. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in8: Imperial Navy Fort IN#8 One of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] , 2nd from the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] side. IN#8 is a large round tower, or tump, with artillery overlooking the western channel.  It is separated from the rest of [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] by a major crevasse, bridged only by the wall connecting it to [[in9|IN#9 - Geometer's Tump]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in9: Imperial Navy Fort IN#9 - Geometer's Tump Third of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] from the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] side, IN#9 is a three staged tower, with heavy artillery overlooking the western approach and the Southern saddle of [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] . Fortifications connect it to [[in10|IN#10 - Fleet House]] , and bridge the crevasse seperating it from [[in8|IN#8]] on the Western heights. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in10: Imperial Navy Fort IN#10 - Fleet House Central blockhouse of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] , on the North Shore of Harbor Island. IN#10 overlooks the primary harbor, controlling it with banks of heavy artillery.  It also houses the bulk of the personnel stationed on [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] , including pilots and sailors of the Narrows protective fleet. The first two floors are an open hall, serving as a market area for the base. The Narrows Bar, a popular drinking establishment, does a rowdy business here, and extends to outdoor tables when the weather is nice. Nevertheless, the walls are thick, the embrasures are well sited, and it remains a high security Imperial facility. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in11: Imperial Navy Fort IN#11 - Harbor Tump Central tump, or round tower, of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . Anchoring the Eastern [[shay_head|Shay Head]] side of [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] , IN#11 mounts heavy artillery overlooking the Harbor and the approach to the Eastern passages.  Fortifications connect it to [[in12|IN#12]] on the Eastern heights. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in12: Imperial Navy Fort IN#12 Built on the towering heights on the Eastern end of [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] , Tump 12 has a wide field of fire bearing on the Eastern approaches of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . Third from the [[shay_head|Shay Head]] side, IN#12 also secures the Eastern fortifications on [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] , which connect it to [[in11|IN#11]] .  IN#12 mounts more heavy artillery than any other single tump, because of its fields of fire. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in13: Imperial Navy Fort IN#13 Built on the heights of Herders' Rock, IN#13 is the second Easternmost of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] in the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . Its artillery overlooks the Eastern passages seperating it from the Eastern end of [[harbor_island|Harbor Island]] and the Western point of [[shay_head|Shay Head]] . The tower is supplied by vast winches on the lower Northern cliffs, where there are fair weather docks. A great herd of shaggy cattle, feeding the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] , are raised here.  Grapevines do well, and a small winery operates here, again primarily serving those stationed in the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in14: Imperial Navy Fort IN#14 Easternmost of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] across the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] , IN#14 is built on the Western point of [[shay_head|Shay Head]] . Strong fortifications extend to the landward approaches. Heavy artillery and a squadron guard the Eastern passages. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in15: Imperial Navy Fort IN#15 Map: P21 Fortified lighthouse on the Southernmost  tip of [[codya_point|Codya Point]] , a Southward jut of land on the Western flank of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] .  It has a breakwall to make the best of a harbor with too much Southern exposure, but in a real Southerly storm, the squadron may have to shelter in the cut some 20 miles NNW in [[jojojopo_forest_bay|Jojojopo Forest Bay]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in16: Imperial Navy Fort IN#16 Map: Q23 Fortified lighthouse on the most Southerly of the [[jojojopo_rocks|Jojojopo Rocks]] , warning [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] traffic.  There is a surprising sized fort, allowing the sheepherders and fishermen who make their home on the Rocks to take shelter, though Ships too big to pull ashore have to shelter inland of the largest of the Rocks or beat North to harbor in the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in17: Imperial Navy Fort IN#17 Map: P23 Fortified lighthouse on [[shay_head|Shay Head]] , guarding the Eastern approach to the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] and thence the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] .  A breakwall improves an adequate small harborage on the inland side. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in18: Imperial Navy Yard IN#18 The Narrows Yard Map: P22 The Narrows Yard is a major shipyard in a huge naturally well protected harbor on the West bank of the Dargonesti Narrows, with the harbor mouth facing North toward the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] .  Large ocean going vessels can be piloted or tugged through the channels, but they can also do business here without paying the significant Passage Tax to gain access to the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] . This serves several purposes, limiting foreign traffic inside the sound, and allowing the Free Imperia to trade at better rates at a central Ocean port facility where they can load 'Jammers and distribute as needed throughout the Empire.  The Free Imperia makes no secret that Merchants can barter for better prices inside, after paying the tax, and paying taxes on the goods that they bring out, but the convenience of the deep water port tempts many sea-weary Captains.  Others may anchor here in the lanes, and take part of their cargo into the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] in a smaller hull, many of which are for hire. The yard can repair wet hulls and SpellJammers, and constructs small fisher boats, tug galleys for the channel, and large ocean going vessels.  It is rumored amongst those in the know to be a primary refitting yard for Q-Ships. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in19: Imperial Navy Fort IN#19 Map: P22-Q22 A fortified lighthouse built on the Southernmost tip of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] , about 35 miles due south from [[in18|IN#18]] .  A poor small harbor 10 miles to the west shelters a few fishing boats. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in20: Imperial Navy Fort IN#20 Smuggler's Cove Map: P23 A fortified lighthouse on the Easternmost point of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] , guarding the Western edge of the entrance to the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] .  It's well protected harbor surrounded by forest is colloquially known as Smuggler's Cove, though whether the name was first applied to the local rum distillery and bar or the Harbor itself is a matter of some debate.  Despite its rowdy reputation there is a significant protective squadron stationed here. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in21: Imperial Navy Fort IN#21 Map: Q24 A fortified lighthouse on the southernmost tip of the [[tri_king_mountains|Tri-King Mountains]] , at the very end of the [[tri_king_peninsula|Tri-King Peninsula]] . There is a poor harbor improved by a breakwall 20 miles to the North with a Dwarven tavern that caters to the off duty sailors. It is a bleak and barren point of land and the tavern does more business than its Dwarven Sea Stout really justifies - its a good beer, but there isn't much else to do.  In case of heavier storms than the harbor can handle the fleet can shelter just up the Peninsula in the harbor of [[dk4|Dwarf Kings Outpost DK#4]] , or further North at [[dk2|Dwarf Kings Outpost #2]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in22: Imperial Navy Ouptost IN#22 Map: N23 The fortifications on the [[stronghold_river|Stronghold River]] mouth into the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] formed the core of [[king_cormach|King Cormach]] 's Eastern Capital, [[harnia|Harnia]] , the gateway to the East.  In addition to the the Naval batteries covering the River Mouth, there is now a large port and fortified city with their own batteries. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in23: Imperial Navy Yard IN#23 East Harbor Naval Yard Map: N21 East Harbor Naval Yard. This is a well fortified but sprawling shipyard on [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] between the mouths of the [[east_river|East River]] and the [[jojojopo_river|Jojojopo River]] . While 'Jammer construction is kept inside the Sister Cities, any lesser task is being performed here regularly. Riverboats, Ocean going vessels, and smaller craft are built in large numbers, and anything at all can be repaired. Cargo from, or headed for, the Jojojopo River is bought, sold, processed and upgraded. Millwheels grind grain, weave fabric, and power workshops. One of the largest ropeworks in the Free Imperia is located here. There are a wide variety of lodgings, taverns, and entertainments, including the East Harbor Rum Distillery. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in24: Imperial Navy Fort #24 Map: P20 This fortified lighthouse on the Southernmost tip of [[olyas_point|Olyas Point]] has a tiny harbor, to which a breakwall adds modest protection.  Except when trading ships pick up fleece from the sheepherders and crafts and ore from the Hill Dwarves, very few outsiders make port here, but the shipping lane offshore stays busy. Some hundred miles WSW of [[in5|Imperial Navy Fort IN#5]] , it separates the [[firth_of_olyas|Firth of Olyas]] from the [[bight_of_exile|Bight of Exile]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in25: Imperial Navy Fort IN#25 Map: L20 [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] Outpost #25 is a small but well fortified port on a wooded harbor on the [[lodenuly_bay|Lōdenūlý Bay]] , on the West shore, SW of the mouth of the [[lodenuly_river|Lōdenūlý River]] at [[samarth|Samarth]] , and NW of where the bay feeds into the [[bight_of_exile|Bight of Exile]] .  It has a good harbor, further improved by a fortified breakwall. In addition to a supplying a scatter of settlements along the river, the coast and in the forest, it sees a fair amount of [[peacekeepers|Paurgiliath Peacekeepers]] traffic between [[pk1|PK#1]] and [[pk3|PK#3]] .  This is a standard training and supply run, both for the Fourth (the Naval Legion), and members of the other Legions training for their Amphibious Rating, as well as Home or Support Legion noncombatants transferring between bases. A pungent gin is made here, under several labels, flavored with the berries or cones of coniferous shrubs indigenous to the local desert. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in26: Imperial Navy Fort IN#26 Map: M22-M23 A fortified lighthouse warns vessels of the rocks off Pyramid Peak Point, on the Western shore of the [[bight_of_exile|Bight of Exile]] , about midway down the [[ivory_peninsula|Ivory Peninsula]] . The single mountain on the point is very pyramid shaped, but seemingly natural in origin.  Among other things it is nearly 12 miles across the base of each remarkably regular side; surely no-one would build a pyramid that big, and if they did it must have been so long ago that sediment completely conceals it. Still, there are local stories of lights moving erratically on the sides of the Pyramid late on moonless nights.  One persistent rumor is that secret governmental projects take place there, though other versions attribute the lights to ghosts, mysterious rituals, or lost underground civilizations. A modest but cheerful village has accreted around it as the Western Settlements have grown.  They make a variety of good cider, home stilled scumble, and Pyramid Applejack and Brandy from the orchards that dot the Point. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in27: Imperial Navy Fort IN#27 Map: O21 A prosperous inland port on the Southeastern shore of Lake Jojojopo, at the headwaters of the [[jojojopo_river|Jojojopo River]] , surrounded by a beautiful mix of different terrains.  A variety of Gruits and Ales are made here, though none have risen to prominence. The Lakeside Sumac is said to be quite tasty, but is made in limited quantities. It's said that between the different settlements in the mountains, the forests, and the rolling hills, it isn't uncommon to see as diverse a crowd as you would in the capital. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in28: Imperial Navy Base IN#28 Map: R20 Naval Base #28 was built on Horseshoe Rock, a 50 odd mile wide remnant of a long extinct volcano. Gently rolling hills surround an ideal caldera harbor, its narrow entrance guarded by a shoal of three small islands with artillery forts. Added to this, it has a small but steady freshwater spring welling up from unimaginable depths. It is, in point of fact, as if [[church_of_eru|Eru]] designed it specifically for the [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperial Navy]] to anchor the safety of the [[southern_archipelago|archipelago]] from. The huge Naval Fortification was designed and stocked to supply and safeguard island shipping and settlements. Only frigates and smaller ships are built in the yards, but they are more than capable of repairs on anything that floats or flies. The fort has been worked with a system of channels so that vessels may be moved rapidly across the island from the harbor and launched on the other side. The island's volcanic soil grows remarkable Shiraz grapes, and its vinters are justifiably famous. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in29: Imperial Navy Fort IN#29 Map: P17 A strong fort guards the excellent natural harbor at the mouth of the [[chennacatt_river|Chennacatt River]] onto the [[bight_of_exile|Bight of Exile]] .  A sizable squadron and garrison is stationed here to protect the river traffic taking the [[inland_waterway|Great Inland Waterway Initiative]] shortcut through [[iron_fist|Iron Fist]] or [[citadel_city|Citadel City]] . The excellent forest surrounding has led to many Harnic and some Krynnic elves settling nearby. A very passable Chenacatt Lager is made locally, and frequently served with citrus slices that keep flies from crawling into the neck of the bottle. There is good trade in nuts and fruits, local pottery, and goods brought from longer distance. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in30: Imperial Navy Fort IN#30 Map: N27 A fortified lighthouse and artillery battery guarding the Southern point of the Arg-Simorig gap into [[grand_monaco_bay|Grand Monaco Bay]] .  A small harbor is built into the lee of the point, enhanced by a breakwall. The Southern point is home to a Monestary of [[church_of_eru|Eru]] , primarily devoted to the studies of astronomy offered by the great open [[eastern_ocean|Eastern Ocean]] .  The monks also make Starry Night Absinthe.  A number of young adults from the capitol come here to study; primarily though not exclusively of Elven descent, and much of the forest is rigged with platforms and elevated pathways.  A scattering of natives, a small dark haired folk of an appearance between proto-polynesian and proto-pictish, have friendly relations with the monastery and students, and serve as regular guest lecturers.  In addition to exceptional knowledge of local fauna, flora and geography, their people have a strong oral tradition in the astronomy of [[places_on_arda#ardaspace_sphere|ArdaSpace]] .  Their children are well trained in navigation of their dugouts and catamarans by stars alone, and their 'star-mother' priestess caste have cultivated an exceptional ability to do calculations and memorization, particularly of astronomical objects and periods.  They are few in number, though small bands of their kin are scattered along the Eastern seabord of Arda.  They had historically been picked on by land dwelling neighbors when they come to shore, and are very friendly to the [[start|Free Imperia]] , particularly fascinated by the ships and Spelljammers they build. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in31: Imperial Navy Fort IN#31 Map: N26 A fortified lighthouse and artillery battery guarding the Northern point of the Arg-Simorig gap into [[grand_monaco_bay|Grand Monaco Bay]] . A small harbor is built into the lee of the point, enhanced by a breakwall. Some of [[barony_munchausen|Barony Munchausen]] 's famous alpaca farms and orchards range Northwards along the point. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in32: Imperial Navy Fort IN#32 Map: M24 A strong island fortress in [[great_stronghold_lake|Great Stronghold Lake]] , with breakwalls creating small harbors on multiple sides.  It garrisons and supplies the bulk of the Imperial Military and Naval forces assigned to the Stronghold Lakes region. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in33: Imperial Navy Base IN#33 Map: O14 Built to protect the [[dushera_bight|Dûshera Bight]] and the [[bay_of_usakan|Bay of Ûsakan]] , IN#33 does a good job of defending its island fortress, and some surrounding Naval traffic. It was supplemented by [[in35|IN#35]] , and today is more focused on patrolling for deep-water threats than the bays themselves. There is a thriving bit of Imperial civilization on the island itself, with lush gardens, tropical fruits, and bright plumaged birds. Sugarcane is farmed, along with citrus and nut trees. The local distillery hosts theatrical and musical events, particularly striving to attract talent from [[nexus_prime:start|Nexus Prime]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in34: Imperial  Navy Fort IN#34 Map: R13 This river fort on the [[bay_of_usakan|Bay of Ûsakan]] defends and supplies the last river leg of the Free Imperia's [[inland_waterway|great inland waterway]] . Guarding the Eastern end of the Thanihazad bypass, the fort sees a lot of traffic, and is heavily engineered and supplied.  It maintains a significant wet-hull fleet, which with the [[rainbow_barbarians|Rainbow Barbarians]] , keeps the surrounding bay neutral or friendly, suppressing pirates, and maintaining naval superiority in the region. A sizable [[free_imperia_navy#marines_personnel|Marine]] contigent, along with coordination with the [[rainbow_barbarians|Rainbow Barbarians]] and [[peacekeepers|Paurgiliath Peacekeepers]] forces in the area, and mobile force deployments from the [[signal_company|Signal Company]] , [[watc|West Arda Trading Company]] , and [[imperial_officeholders_and_appointees|Imperial Military]] allows regular patrols of the riverbanks and surrounding forest.  Relationships with locals are generally good, and steadily improving, largely due to the twin doctrines of overwhelming force and improved standards of living. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in35: Imperial Navy Ouptost IN#35 Map: N15-O15 Built on the mouth of the [[dushera_bight|Dûshera Bight]] to support the smaller [[in33|IN#33]] , [[lancelot|Lancelot Du Lac]] was once heard to compare IN#35 to 'Borneo in the Earlies'.  Whatever he meant, it is a vibrant if troubled region. Trade is rich, naval traffic is abundant, but seemingly endless small tribes of pirates and headhunters live in the deep jungle between the [[bay_of_usakan|Bay of Ûsakan]] and the [[dushera_bight|Dûshera Bight]] (at the mouth of the [[koros_river|Koros River]] ), and limiting their maritime depredations is all that a Naval force can achieve. It will be Elven generations before the [[rainbow_barbarians|Rainbow Barbarians]] grow enough to push them out, and while they are no particular threat to the fort, they continue their audacious raids on lone unwary shipping. Q-ships are helpful, but the problem is less in deterring an organized power than in diverse bloodthirsty small groups which may turn hostile, or not, on any given week. Many of the more peaceful tribes have gathered near the fort, or near the Barbarians in the North, but it will be some time before the deep jungle is truly pacified. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in36: Imperial Navy Fort IN#36 Map: S18 This strong if small [[free_imperia_navy|Naval]] Fort secures the mouth of the [[bay_of_gan|Bay of Gan]] , separating the [[ivory_peninsula|Ivory Peninsula]] from the [[mumakan_peninsula|Mûmakan Peninsula]] . Generally a quiet posting, it still maintains a strong harbor and fleet, and patrols a large area. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in37: Imperial Navy Fort IN#37 Map: K28 This fortified lighthouse and harbor at the Southern entrance to the [[gulf_of_the_firstborn|Gulf of the Firstborn]] acts as a waypoint for shipping to and from the great [[imperial_timber_operation|Imperial timber]] fort at [[in39|IN#39]] . Generally a desolate posting apart from the [[free_imperia_navy|Naval]] traffic, the rocky island is primarily inhabited by seals, walrus, puffins, and other seabirds. Occasional bear, elk, catamounts, and moose swim across from the larger island of Thuriat Codya. Deep sea whales, largely sieve feeders, and Narwhal, are often seen offshore. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in38: Imperial Navy Fort IN#38 Map: I28 In addition to protecting the narrows leading to the [[gulf_of_the_firstborn|Gulf of the Firstborn]] , this [[free_imperia_navy|Naval]] Fortress acts as a coordination point for shipping entering and leaving [[in39|IN#39]] .  Dolphins are common here, along with great predatory black and white whales. [[red_mountains|Red Mountains]] [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in39: Imperial Navy Fort IN#39 Map: I28 The great Northern [[imperial_timber_operation|Imperial Timber Operation]] of the Free Imperia is always a bustle of activity.  Selective foresting here, guided by an Elven ethic of preservation, still supplies much of the Empire with wood. Outlying camps selectively cut, coppice, and reforest.  Raw logs are sledged, carted, or barged to bring the timber to the great fort's seasoning sheds and milling works.  Processed timber is assembled into shiploads. Timber shipping is organized into protective squadrons or fleets at [[in38|IN#38]] , and sent to the Sister Cities via the Eastern half of the [[inland_waterway|Great Inland Waterway Initiative]] . The misty Northern climate breeds hardy natives, who mostly welcome the trade and opportunity that the Free Imperia brings to the region.  Pelts, amber, news of the Northlands, and other native trade goods find their way regularly to the WATC offices here. Jammer and Wet-hull repairs are regularly undertaken here, as is construction of timber barges and merchant ships. Regular supply runs travel over the [[red_mountains|Red Mountains]] to the archeological works on the possible site of the first Elven awakening at [[ce1|Church of Eru Arda Heritage Site CE#1]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in40: Imperial Navy Ouptost IN#40 Map: Q12 Built on the historic site of Kharadûn, guarding the mouth of the [[norpul_river|Norpûl Estuary]] , IN#40 is the Westernmost outpost of the Empire. It anchors the end of the Free Imperia's [[inland_waterway|inland waterway]] which cuts thousands of miles off sailing around the uttermost South. The local jungle tribes are strongly pro-empire, as it provides them with protection from their more warlike neighbors to the North. The [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] keeps several strong squadrons here, as their primary port on the Western Ocean. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in41: IN#41 Map: L26 The naval fort and lighthouse on the tip of [[long_claw_point|Longclaw Point]] guards the Northern end of the entrance to the [[great_silvanesti_bay|Great Sylvanesti Bay]] , and the Southern approach to the [[kagonesti_basin|Kagonesti Basin]] . Wading birds migrate through in great numbers, along with ducks, and sea lions have a large, well established rookery here. A strong harbor is breakwalled inside the point, with a significant  protective squadron. Traffic on the [[inland_waterway|Great Inland Waterway]] routinely rounds the point between legs.  To the North, the [[silver_river|Silver River]] brings barges of Imperial Timber down from [[argentum_capita|Argentum Capita]] through the [[kagonesti_basin|Kagonesti Basin]] , and Southern lines enter [[great_silvanesti_bay|Great Sylvanesti Bay]] at [[new_silvan|New Silvan]] and [[semboch|Semboch]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
in42: IN#42 Map: L26 A fortified lighthouse and harbor on [[breakshell_bank|Breakshell Bank]] , the Northern terminus of the [[tri_king_mountains|Tri-King Mountains]] , IN#42 guards the southern point of the entrance to [[great_silvanesti_bay|Great Sylvanesti Bay]] . There are a variety of edible crustaceans here, including a cream and blue shelled lobster, gathered by shallow bottom boats that work over and between the sand and rock bars. The several small bays to the south are particularly rich in them, and several small villages of lobstermen have grown up, delivering their daily catch to [[semboch|Semboch]] and [[new_silvan|New Silvan]] . [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
independent_vessels: Independent Vessels [[moonslayer_arrowing|Moonslayer (Arrowing)]] , Owned and Run By [[captain_silvereye_rinronnniallelas|Captain Silvereye Rin'ron'nniallelas]] - N(G) Drow Captain in the Spidermoon Sector [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] [[watc_navy|WATC Fleet]]
indigo_rock_barbarians: Indigo Rock Barbarians The Indigo Rock Barbarians are Harnic Elves in origin, and are one tribe of the [[rainbow_barbarians|Rainbow Barbarians]] . [[chieftain_baluzn_giallarileithan|Chieftain Baluz'n Giallarileithan]] - Barbarian Fighter L7 CG Harnic High Elf - leads the Indigo Rock Barbarians and their totem is Lizard. Sub-Chieftain Baluz’n (Lizard) (B7) Belli (D3) Huzzalisthalista (Cl3) – Ilúvatar
infyrana: Infyrana Infyrana is an evil Red Dragon that [[party|The Party]] thwarted, who fled [[arda:start|Arda]] with her plane hopping mountain. Infyrana's character sheet
inland_waterway:
Great Inland Waterway Initiative [[places_on_arda#west_arda_trading_company|TC#1]] with Lock Tankers The various nations of the Free Imperia have cooperated with [[imperial_officeholders_and_appointees|Imperial Engineers]] , the [[field_engineering_corps|Field Engineering Corps]] , and the [[fortification_initiative|Fortification Initiative]] to cut thousands of miles off cross-continental shipping routes, particularly from the [[imperial_timber_operation|Imperial Timber Operation]] in the NE through rivers to the Westernmost [[free_imperia_navy|Imperial Navy]] Ouptost near Thanihazad.
The functional engineering solution was to connect the navigable headwaters of different watersheds via flying Lock Tankers, which carry shipping from one to the other. These Lock Tankers are essentially giant stone troughs, with a tree fort at one end, produced by the [[fortification_initiative|Fortification Initiative]] and enchanted with the 9th level wizard spell Sky Castle, allowing them to fly at a walking pace.  The tanker submerges the trough in fortified Sky Lock reservoirs, takes on or discharges shipping, then flies to the next Sky Lock.
irda_tree: Irda Tree Once a sacred tree of the Sylvanesti elves of Krynn, she was polymorphed into a red haired half-elf illusionist of great power by [[seth|Seth]] , an avatar of the Chaos God 'God of Everything and Nothing', and moved to Nexus Prime. She is revered by the Silvanesti, and by the [[druid_circle|Druid Circles of Arda]] . Some of her aged Silvanesti caretakers call her Laurelin. Irda is a member of the [[order_magika_mage_college|Order Magika]] . Illusionist L19 CN Half Elf Irda's character sheet as an .odt Irda's character sheet as a .rtf
iron_fist: Iron Fist Iron Fist - Map: Q16 The Spice Streets - ethnography,  flora, fauna tin ore vein, iron ore vein Founded and ruled by the [[three_kings_of_the_dwarves|Three Kings of the Dwarves]] Iron Fist is a mostly Harnic Dwarf fortress, though those of Krynnic, Faerun,  native or other stock are welcome. It is the greatest armory of the dwarfholds, crafting weapons and armor not only for their own folk, but for the [[solamnic_raiders|Solamnic Orders]] , and some for [[king_cormach|Cormach]] and [[duke_rocha|Rocha]] 's folk as well. It has a Temple of the [[church_of_eru|Church of Eru Ilùvatar]] .  With its typical interfaith cooperation, this includes a wing with shrines of: [[church_of_moradin|Church of Moradin]] [[church_of_dumathoin|Church of Dumathoin]] [[church_of_gorm|Church of Gorm]] [[church_of_reorx|Church of Reorx]] They operate a Lock-tanker shuttle between watersheds on either side of the [[yellow_mountains|Yellow Mountains]] , adding river traffic to an ancient trade route, connecting Isra and the Highland Lake region of Gan. They breed the local Water Buffalo for food, milk, transportation, and use them on treadmills and turnstiles to power their machinery.  They harvest local herbs, and are renowned for their healing lore. In particular, a moss which only grows on a local shrub is sovereign against many illnesses, but loses all value when no longer fresh, becoming toxic.  A local river tuber, mashed into a poultice, speeds the healing of muscle and bone injuries. They ferment sugarcane, often with a local star-shaped flower with stimulant properties. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
isaak_kang_ying: Isaak Kang Ying Isaak Kang Ying is an Arch Druid of the Torillean [[druid_circle|Druid Circle of Arda]] . Druid(Beastfriend) L13 N Human Isaak Kang Ying's character sheet
istari:
The Istari Maiar of [[church_of_eru|Eru]] The Wizards, commonly known as the Istari (Quenya) and the Ithryn (Sindarin) was the title assigned to five [[church_of_eru#the_maiar|Maiar]] in the Third Age of Middle-earth. They formed the Order of Wizards (Q. Heren Istarion) . Among Men it was initially assumed that the Wizards were also men who, by long and secret study, had acquired great knowledge of lore and arts. However, as the Third Age passed it was marked that the Wizards did not die, so Men began to believe that they were of Elven-kind. However, none except Elrond, Círdan, and Galadriel knew that, in actuality, the Wizards were vassals of the [[church_of_eru#the_valar|Valar]] who were sent to assist the Free peoples of Middle-earth against Sauron as he gathered his forces during the Third Age. Formation of The Order
The five known Istari were: Curumo, a Maia of [[aule|Aulë]] , the chief and the wisest of the Order according to Gandalf during the Council of Elrond. Olórin, a Maia of [[manwe|Manwë]] and [[varda|Varda]] (held by Círdan the Shipwright to be the wisest of the Order). Aiwendil, a Maia of [[yavanna|Yavanna]] ; also known as Hrávandil. Two Wizards who went into the East and South, and do not appear in any of the main tales of Middle-earth. The names Alatar and Pallando, both Maiar of [[orome|Oromë]] are known. However there are tales about two Wizards, perhaps the same two, called Rómestámo and Morinehtar who operated during the Second Age. It is not known whether they are the same spirits as Palacendo and Haimenar. The precursor of the Heren Istarion were perhaps the Five Guardians, who, under [[melian|Melian]] , were tasked by the Valar to protect the first Elves during the Battle of the Powers; the spirits assigned for this corresponded more or less to the Maiar who were sent millennia later. The Heren Istarion had been created in [[valinor|Valinor]] . A council of the Valar was called by Manwë which resolved to send three emissaries. Initially only Curumo, chosen by Aulë, and Alatar, chosen by Oromë, stepped forward. Manwë then asked for Olórin and commanded him to go. Curumo took Aiwendil with him because Yavanna begged him to do so and Alatar took along his friend Pallando. They were clothed in the bodies of old men, restricting their powers so that they would only assist the peoples of Middle-earth and not seek dominion like Sauron, who was also a Maia. They were charged by the Valar to assist the people of Middle-earth through persuasion and encouragement, not force or fear. By inhabiting the bodies of Men they also became susceptible to all of the weaknesses of a physical body: they felt hunger, pain, greed, sorrow, joy, and all other emotions and pains of Men. While they were vulnerable and they could be killed, they aged only very slowly and were immortal. Arrival in Middle-earth
Círdan witnessed the arrival of the Order in Middle-earth around the year c. T.A. 1000 (though the two Wizards may have arrived much earlier). Their “mission” was to advise and persuade Men and Elves to resist Sauron. Each wizard was assigned a colour for his clothes. The wizard in white was Saruman, regarded by all as the leader of the order, with white being indicative of the chief. The Wizard clad in brown was Radagast and the one clad in grey was Gandalf, seemingly the oldest and the least of the Order. The other two who travelled to the East and South were sometimes said to clad themselves in robes of sea-blue and were known as the Blue Wizards. It is not known if the colour had any special meaning concerning their rank, abilities or nature. In the northwest of Middle-earth Curumo became known as Saruman to Men and Curunír to Elves; Olórin was known as Gandalf to Men and Mithrandir to Elves; while Aiwendil became known as Radagast. In spite of their specific and unambiguous goal, the Wizards were nevertheless capable of mortal, even negative feelings. Thus, Gandalf felt great affection for the Hobbits and Radagast for the animals. On the other hand, Saruman fell victim to greed, jealousy, and lust for power; the other two Wizards may have also fallen prey to these temptations during their journeys in the East. Very few of Middle-earth's inhabitants knew who the Wizards really were, as the Istari did not share this information. Most believed they were Elves or wise Men; the name Gandalf represents this interpretation, meaning Wand-elf, because the Men who gave him the nickname believed he was an Elf. They attracted few questions due to their gentle nature and dislike of direct interference with other people's affairs.

jarlaxle: Jarlaxle Jarlaxle is a Drow Blademaster. F(Blademaster) L17 NE Drow Jarlaxle's character sheet Character History Little is known of Jarlaxle's past, but he has led Bregan D'aerthe for more than 70 years. Jarlaxle and his band played into the downfall of not one but two noble houses during that time. When House Hun'ett attacked Do'Urden, the attacking drow were supported by Bregan D'aerthe, even while Jarlaxle was in the presence of Matron Malice Do'Urden. She made the rogue drow a better offer, and in the middle of the battle, Bregan D'aerthe switched sides, ensuring the end of house Hun'ett. Jarlaxle and Bregan D'aerthe were also involved in the massive drow force that attacked Mithral Hall under the leadership of Matron Mother Baenre. While the matron mother and several other Baenre females where killed in the failed attack, Jarlaxle the ultimate survivor came through unscathed. Recently Jarlaxle has usurped power in all the underworld operations in the city of Calimport, putting his “friend” Artemis Entreri as his human liason in charge of the assassins guild. With this newfound power, Jarlaxle has spread his influence towards other drow cities. And his operatives have found a book of power and an artifact of incredible power. The book is being translated by Gromph Baenre the Archmage of Menzoberranzan. Most of the pieces of the Crown of Sirius, have been assembled, except for one stone-rumored to be in the Underdeep, somewhere below the Sea of Fallen Stars.

john_constantine: John Constantine John Constantine is a member of the [[order_magika_mage_college|Order Magika]] . [[anita_lesnicki|Anita Lesnicki]] is John Constantine's muscle. Demonologist(Fiend Slayer) L20 CN Human John Constantine's character sheet Character History John's mother died during labour, leaving him to be raised by a father who resented him for simply having been born. Constantine's upbringing was a difficult one - bitter and broken over the loss of his wife, Thomas lost himself in drink and vented his anger upon his hapless young son. John's father hit perhaps his lowest ebb when he was sentenced to six months in prison for stealing women's underwear. John, and his older sister Cheryl, were sent to live with their Aunt Dolly and Uncle Harry. It was here that a still not yet ten years old John Constantine might have been responsible for a second death… While out playing in a field, John stumbled across the half-buried remains of what he thought to be a dead boy. After Finding an odd-coloured stone lodged behind the exposed ribcage of the corpse, Constantine is convinced that his macabre discovery is a fossilized human heart. As time passes John notices a change in his behavior and mood, as he becomes more angry and violent to those around him. Following a harsh exchange with Cheryl, John decides that the 'heart' is cursed and lobs it into a nearby quarry. Constantine's aim proves poor however and it smashes loudly against the tin roof of a shack lived in by a deranged tramp. When the man fails to come outside to investigate the noise, John is sure that the heart has pierced the roof and killed the tramp inside. By the age of fourteen, Constantine had developed an interest in the occult, immersing himself in any books he could find on the subject as a means of escaping the harsh reality of his childhood. Father and son reached a pivotal point in their relationship when John was expelled from school for starting a “Out Demons! Out!” chant at morning assembly. Furious with John's actions, Thomas started a blazing bonfire in their back garden and tossed all of his son's books onto it. So it was that John Constantine was first inspired to use magic to avenge an act of perceived wrong doing against his person. Sifting through the embers of the burnt out bonfire, John was able to salvage a couple of charred, smoke damaged tomes - one of which offered up the perfect means of revenge against his father - a curse that would cause him to waste away and die. Constantine had to kill the next-door neighbour's cat in order to make the curse work, he also had to maim it to make it look like his one-armed father - so he took a razor blade to one of its legs. The deed done, John buried the remains and waited to see what would happen. Much to his surprise, his father fell gravely ill and started to slowly waste away. With Thomas near death, John panicked and went in search of a way to stop the spell but there was none to be found. Finally, acting out of sheer desperation, Constantine exhumed the rotting corpse of the slain cat and stuck it in a jar of formaldehyde. John got lucky, with the corpse now preserved, his father's health stopped deteriorating and while Thomas never made a full recovery, he did survive the experience. One evening during a thunderstorm, John was trying to grab some food from a local bodega, when he was struck by lightning. John up until this point has lead a harsh life and thought during this ill fated moment that it was his judgment day. In a sense it was. When John came to, we was no longer in the City of Angels ( Los Angeles), but in an open field, back dropped with mountains. There was no city, no city lights, no cars, no airplanes. It was an amazingly clear sky. And in looking at the sky, it looked familiar to some degree. He thought that he was in Limbo waiting for judgment. In fact he was in Arda. John through some, luck skill and very possibly some divine intervention eventually made his way to Nexus Prime. Agents at the gate could not understand him, but when an Imperia translator was dispatched it was discovered that he was from an unknown realm called Earth. Mica of the Nine had luckily looked over the reports for that day reading about this person from the realm of Earth and instantly sent for this person for an undisclosed reason.

It is patrolled by squadrons from [[in6|Imperial Navy Fort IN#6]] on [[imperial_point|Imperial Point]] , and less frequently from [[in15|Imperial Navy Fort IN#15]] on [[codya_point|Codya Point]] . jojojopo_peninsula: Jojojopo Peninsula The Jojojopo Peninsula, being the Southern end of the [[ered_ormal_mountains|Ered Ormal]] mountain range, extends Southeast more than 500 miles from the Sister Cities, between the [[east_river|East River]] and [[great_southern_river|Great Southern River]] , forming the Western Shore of [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] and the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] . One of the first areas settled by [[start|The Free Imperia]] ,it is largely secured by [[free_imperia_navy|Naval]] Forts, and held directly by the [[aragorn|Emperor]] . One significant exception is its great port on the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] , the City of [[middle_town|Middle Town]] , founded by Hill Dwarves under the [[three_kings_of_the_dwarves|Three Kings of the Dwarves]] on an exceptional silver mine, which happily exists in the cliffs above a well sheltered broad harbor. On [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] it has the great [[in23|East Harbor Yard, IN#23]] , the largest Naval Yard in the [[start|The Free Imperia]] , built at the mouth of the [[jojojopo_river|Jojojopo River]] , which winds from [[in27|Imperial Navy Fort IN#27]] on lake Jojojopo in the central highlands. [[in3|IN#3]] guards the southern point of [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] 's mouth on the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] , and [[in1|Imperial Navy Fort IN#1]] , built across islands at the Northeastern root of the Jojojopo Peninsula gives the [[east_river|East River]] access to the harbor with drawbridges to control both land traffic and shipping. Proceeding around the coastline from [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] , past [[middle_town|Middle Town]] , we reach [[in7|IN#7]] , which anchors the Western Edge of the [[channel_forts|Channel Forts]] in the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . The furthest Eastern point of the Peninsula has [[in20|IN#20, or Smuggler's Cove]] , another [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] fort with an active village, watching the Western edge of the mouth of the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] .  Just inside the point is the well fortified tax-free harbor of [[in18|IN#18, the Narrows Yard.]] The [[jojojopo_rocks|Jojojopo Rocks]] extend Southeast from the tip, masking the Southern approach to the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] .  The furthest is marked by a [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] fortified lighthouse at [[in16|IN#16]] . [[in19|IN#19]] is a fortified lighthouse on the Southernmost extent of the main Peninsula, and to the West [[in15|IN#15]] is another fortified lighthouse on the southernmost tip of [[codya_point|Codya Point]] . Finally, [[in6|IN#6]] marks the tip of [[imperial_point|Imperial Point]] to the East of the approach to the mouth of the [[great_southern_river|Great Southern River]] where [[in2|Imperial Navy Fort #2]] is the strongly fortified harbor at the Western root of the Peninsula. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
jojojopo_river: Jojojopo River Winding from [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] fort [[in27|IN#27]] at Lake Jojojopo to [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] East Harbor Yard [[in23|IN#23]] on [[east_harbor|East Harbor]] , this is the primary water access to the interior of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] .
jojojopo_rocks: Jojojopo Rocks The Rocks extend Southeast from the tip of the [[jojojopo_peninsula|Jojojopo Peninsula]] , screening the Southern approach to the [[dargonesti_narrows|Dargonesti Narrows]] . [[free_imperia_navy|Free Imperia Navy]] Fort [[in16|IN#16]] warns shipping of the hazards, and provides shelter and protection for the islanders.
jon_architect:
Jon Architect Jon Architect is the [[imperial_officeholders_and_appointees#imperial_counselors|Imperial Architect]] . Jon Architect is a member of the [[order_magika_mage_college|Order Magika]] . Jon is a very well respected academician who has given lectures at the University in Sigil.  He is an accomplished mathematician, architect, geographer, occultist, and consultant to [[aragorn|Aragus Maximus]] , who also devoted much of his life to alchemy, divination, and Hermetic philosophy.  Jon is an ardent promoter of mathematics, a respected engineer and a leading expert in Spelljamming navigation, having trained many of those who would conduct the Imperia's voyages of discovery (he coined the term “Free Empire”). A great source of knowledge, but generally too busy with his own pursuits to be bothered. Scribe(academician) L10 LG Human Jon Architect's character sheet Character History Jon is the Imperial Architect and founder of the Shapers Guild. Although he is not a mage proper, he was raised within academia and is knowledgeable in the academic ways of magic. He is also a respected architect, engineer, and sage. Sage Knowledge: This proficiency represents a specialized area of knowledge or learning. A character with this skill is a fully qualified sage in the area of study chosen and is capable of answering questions concerning the topic after some time spent researching. Naturally, a character may be able to strike a deal with a university, monastery, or wizards' guild hall in order to gain access to their library. Jon has the ability to perform sage research, the character's level of learning allows him to make field observations or attempt to come up with knowledge off the top of his head. For example, a sage who studies botany may attempt a proficiency check in order to identify a particular plant, while one who studies toxicology may be able to identify a poison by its symptoms in a victim. These on-the-spot observations should be limited to information any expert could reasonably come up with in the field - identifying a common gemstone is one thing for a geologist, but making a guess about the electrical conductivity of quartz crystal or the enchantments of a magical gem is a different matter entirely. Purchasing this proficiency at its base cost (2 slots or 5 character points) gives the sage a broad overview of the area of study in question, allowing him to answer general or specific questions in the field. His detailed knowledge allows him to attempt to answer exacting questions in the field. Jon's major fields of study available to a sage include: Architecture: This is the study of the development, theories and styles of architecture. (The architecture proficiency, on the other hand, represents the practical execution of workable building plans.) A sage with this field of study can attempt to identify the age, origins, and general purpose of ruined buildings or structures. Engineering: The character is familiar with the science of building devices, engines, and structures. Sage knowledge of engineering provides a +2 bonus to the character's non-weapon proficiency score in engineering, if he has both proficiencies.
The character can specialize in small machines, large machines (water wheels, etc.), siege engineering, fortifications, bridges and roads, or buildings. Jon's minor fields of study available to a sage include: Art: The sage is familiar with the great works of the past as well as the works of the best contemporary artists. If he specializes in one particular art form (sculpture, paintings, ornamental pottery, etc.) he is able to identify works of the masters, spot fakes, and appraise pieces for sale value. Cartography: Cartography is the art of map-making. A sage who specializes in this field knows where to find maps for any given region or area, knows how to interpret maps using various forms of notation, and can attempt to solve or complete encrypted or partial maps. Mathematics: The study of abstract or theoretical mathematics may seem unusual in a fantasy setting, but it dates back thousands of years in our own world; the ancient Greeks laid the groundwork for geometry, while algebra was a pastime of Islamic scholars and nobles before the European Renaissance. A dimensionalist gains a +2 bonus on his proficiency rating in this area of study. Physics: In most AD&D campaigns, the study of physics centers around mechanics and thermodynamics; some of the more
advanced fields of study simply haven't been invented yet. Unlike other expert hirelings, sages are experts in a single field of academic study. They are most useful to player characters in answering specific questions, solving riddles, or deciphering ancient lore. Jon was hired on a permanent basis in service to the Free Imperia… His own ambitions we set in motion as the designer and guide of a new world so he jumped at the chance to travel and head up a new order of enlightenment. Although he is one of the younger Sages within the Imperia, he is greatly respected and has boundless energy to guide the Imperial Sages and Imperial Shapers Guild. The resources required by the sages can be formidable. At the very least, a sage must have access to a library of considerable size to complete his work. He is not a walking encyclopedia, able to spout facts on command. A sage answers questions by having the right resources at hand and knowing how to use them. The size and quality of the sage's library affect his chance of giving a correct answer. Because of this Jon backs the Imperial Library and Archives. He is also a common visitor within the Order Magica and the new clerical monasteries within the Imperia. Jon can generally answer questions: General 1d6 hours
Specific 1d6 days
Exacting 3d10 days This however drives him away from his designing and personal desires. Because of his stature and intelligence he is generally unapproachable unless there is an Imperial need. He is welcomed within the Imperial court as well as The Order Magica. Jon Architect is a noted mathematician, architect, geographer, occultist, and consultant to Aragus Maximus. He also devoted much of his life to alchemy, divination, and Hermetic philosophy. Because of this Jon can cast magic with use of scrolls. Jon straddles the worlds of science and magic just as they were becoming distinguishable. One of the most learned men of the current era, he has lectured to crowded halls at the magic university of Sigil when still in his early twenties. Jon was an ardent promoter of mathematics, a respected engineer and a leading expert in spelljamming navigation, having trained many of those who would conduct the Imperia's voyages of discovery (he coined the term “Free Empire”).
josh_orcman_the_paladin:
Josh Orcman the Paladin Josh Orcman is an Imperial Paladin of [[church_of_yahshua|Yahshua]] who worships at all the good aligned temples and has sworn vassalage directly to the [[aragorn|Emperor]] .  Kicked out of his tribe of orcs as a child for not fitting in, he was raised by good hearted brewer monks. He has a great personality, stays cheerful, and particularly loves Kender. [[julianne_the_half_orc|Julianne the Half Orc]] is in love with Josh Orcman, and follows him wherever he goes. P(Chevalier) L7 LG Half Orc Josh Orcman's character sheet Character History Josh has an extremely good personality, Sure he knows he is a half orc, but he has never let that get him down. His personality rose above anything bad that has ever happened and he remained a “kid” all his life. He especially loves the Kendar kind and will go out of his way to help and protect them. Thanks to his sunny personality, broad pantomime, clever impersonations it is easy to forget that Josh is an Orc… People know very little about him, but he has hinted that he was cast away from his clan at a very young age because he just did not fit in. He was taken in by a set of Monks and taught their was, mostly brewing beer and learning the ways of the humans. He liked them, they were kind and genial sorts. They often tried to hide him, but his rubber face and fast patter were an instant hit. Often he would entertain the monks with songs and jokes. Although many monks thought he would be a great bard, initial reactions to a 1/2 orc were not so good and his natural ability to fight also played a role. He thought to become a mercenary and adventurer, but soon he realized that he wanted to be on the side of good. He knows the ways of Paladine, Yahshua, Ilúvatar and all the Imperial gods of good, and he worships them all. He prays every day for his path to become clear. Josh can often be found where
ever there are Kendar… Doing their heavy work. He also has a natural 50% chance to detect pick pocketing from the many hours spent with them. Josh is mild mannered and always aware of how humans will react to him… he hides behind jokes and meekness when able… but never shies away from a fight if attacked first. He does not like evil things and will never hide among normal orcs for any reason. He has sworn fidelity to Aragorn because of his fairness, openness to talk with him and his obvious like of his Kendar friends.
julianne_the_half_orc: Julianne the Half Orc Julianne the Half Orc is in love with [[josh_orcman_the_paladin|Josh Orcman the Paladin]] and follows him wherever he goes. Thief L7 CN Half Orc Julianne's character sheet Character History Julianne the Half Orc loves Josh Orcman the Palidin… and goes out of her way to make sure he does not make a fool of himself.  He is so kind hearted she hates it when he is made fun of. She loves him for how he is able to forgive, but secretly hates her Orc side… She has vowed to wait for Josh to fall in love with her, although he seems ever dense. Julianne watches Josh's back and often does things to make sure he does not have to see the seedier side of life… She has leaned a lot of thief skills from living with Josh among the Kender which she sometimes does for her own gain… In the end - She will always follow her Warrior, to hell and back.

karsellyn_lylyl_lytherraias: Karsel'lyn Lylyl-Lytherraias Karsel'lyn Lylyl-Lytherraias is the Drow Ambassador to [[queen_amlaruil_moonflower_the_sad_queen|Queen Amlaruil Moonflower (The Sad Queen)]] of Evermeet. Cleric(Diplomat) L12 CG Drow Karsel'lyn Lylyl-Lytherraias' character sheet Character History Lady Karsel'lyn Lylyl-Lytherraias's presence on the isle of [[locations#realmspace_sphere|Evermeet]] is a secret shared only by her, the [[queen_amlaruil_moonflower_the_sad_queen|queen]] , and [[laeroth_runemaster|Laeroth Runemaster]] , the master high mage. Karsel'lyn is a priestess of the good Drow goddess, Eilistraee, and has in the past been one of [[queen_amlaruil_moonflower_the_sad_queen|Queen Amlaruil]] 's best agents among the dark ones in the Realms. Now she is on Evermeet, discussing what would have been, until recently, thought impossible the possibility that the Drow worshippers of Eilistraee would be allowed to follow the Retreat to [[locations#realmspace_sphere|Evermeet]] . Lady Karsel'yn Lylyl-Lytherraias is as graceful as her name, and is the perfect representative of the tiny group of Drow who have forsaken the evil and decadence of the lower realms and embraced the loving and naturistic worship of Eilistraee. In general outlook, she is much like a Grey elf. She is impulsive, chaotic, intense, flirtatious, and somewhat fickle. Karsel'lyn faces an uphill struggle in her mission. Although [[queen_amlaruil_moonflower_the_sad_queen|Amlaruil]] values her as an agent and a friend, she knows that the conservative Gold elves will never accept Drow on [[locations#realmspace_sphere|Evermeet]] . The Silver elves may be more inclined to at least consider the possibility that some Drow have turned away from the ways of the evil gods, but even they are suspicious. Unknown to Lady Karsel'lyn, several Drow families have hired a Drow assassin named Mourn to hunt her down and kill her, thus ending any current moves toward reconciliation between the elves and the worshipers of Eilistraee. Some observers have suggested that the Drow lady is a rival of the druidess Aerilaya for the affections of Captain Carreigh Macumail, but none of the principals in the matter have ever discussed it publicly.
kat_tejeomare: Kat Tejeomare Kat Tejeomare is a court mage for [[king_cormach|King Cormach]] . Kat Tejeomare is a member of the [[order_magika_mage_college|Order Magika]] MU L12 CG Human Kat's character sheet Unique Spells by Kat Tejeomare [[kat_tejeomare|Kat Tejeomare]] Kat Tejeomare's Flaming Vortex AKA: Fellstar's Flaming Vortex (Evocation) Level:  3 Range:  10 yards per level Components:  V, S, M Duration:  1 round per level Casting Time:  3 Area of Effect:  8´2 feet vertical cone Saving Throw:  ½ This spell calls into being a spinning vortex of flames that resembles a burning dust devil; the vortex is 8 feet high and 2 feet wide at its widest. The caster may direct the movement of the vortex in any direction desired, but it may not be moved across a body of water. The vortex moves at a rate of 10 feet per round, and the caster must maintain full concentration in order to direct its movements; if the caster loses concentration, the vortex will move in a straight line at full movement rate until the caster can again gain concentration. The wizard may not move the vortex further away than 10 yards per level of the caster, or the spell terminates. The caster may use the vortex to attack a single victim per round; he may attack the same target in following rounds, or may elect to move the vortex to attack a different one. Anyone struck by the vortex suffers 1d4 points of damage per level of the caster (up to a maximum of 10d4). A successful saving throw versus spell reduces this damage by half. The flames from this spell will ignite flammable materials on contact, but will not harm most other materials, unless exposure is prolonged. That is, if a creature is attacked by the vortex for only a single round, non-flammable possessions are not affected; if attacked on two consecutive rounds, all possessions must save versus magical fire normally (but only if the target fails his saving throw). Each additional round of exposure inflicts a -1 on all possessions' saving throws (no penalty in added to the target's saving throw). The material component for this spell is a piece of flammable material suspended from a string; the caster lights the material on fire and twirls it in a circle while casting the spell. He must continue doing this throughout the duration of the spell, and the material must remain lit; if it does not, the spell ends prematurely. (Source: GNSB, Author:  Fellstar) Kat Tejeomare's Shout of Ruin AKA: Shout of Ruin (Invocation/Evocation) Level: 6 Area of Effect:	Cone, 50 ft long, 20 ft diameter Casting Time: 6 Components: V, S Duration: Instant Range: 0 Saving Throw: Special Shout of ruin is similar to the 4th-level shout spell, but more powerful; booming forth a shout of ruin spell creates a magical wave of violently destructive sonic force that issues from the mouth of the caster like the bass toll of doom.  The sonic blast is channeled from the mouth of the caster in the shape of a cone that reaches 50 feet in length and 20 feet in diameter at the far end.  Beyond the area of effect, the deep boom of the shout of ruin is painfully audible.  In the area of effect, the sound stuns creatures for 2 rounds, deafens for 4 rounds, and inflicts 2d6 point of damage.  Those making a successful saving throw vs. spell take half damage, are deafened for 2 rounds, and are not stunned at all. Objects of lesser sturdiness and strength than stone walls of 6-inch thickness (or wooden walls of 1-foot thickness) must make a successful item saving throw vs. crushing blow or be destroyed.  Normal doors are blown apart and even reinforced or barred doors of normal size are blown open.  Objects not subject to immediate destruction are damaged - the sound cracks and splinters most surfaces to some degree.  Persistent application of this spell will slowly erode even the stoutest of barriers at a rate decided by the DM. A solid physical object of sturdy construction and at least 3 inches thick that survives the shout of ruin can completely shield an individual taking total cover behind it from stunning and damage (but not deafness).  Directing this spell at a large window, on the other hand, will cause it to shatter in a lethal spray of glass shrapnel away from the caster, with potential damage to those caught in the area assigned by the DM (which should not exceed 2d6 points of additional damage). This spell is debilitating.  The wizard must pass an immediate system shock check after casting the shout of ruin or be rendered unconscious for 2d8 turns. (From College of Wizardry by TSR, page #82)

kelestia:
The Keléstia The Keléstia The Keléstia is a collective of seven linked parallel worlds in the family of Terra.  The planets of  Earth,  Arda (Tolkien's Middle-earth), Narnia (C.S. Lewis), Kèthîra (Harn), Oerth, Uerth, and Toril. All seven are linked
through Planescape.   Not everything is exact, however under the high power, all the gods of Earth exist - the Norse gods, the Finnish gods, the Chinese and Indian gods, all sorts of pantheons who often bear the names of Earthly
nations.  Due to time distortions of language differences gods sometimes have differnt names, but many times can be traced to the gods of other planes.  One could argue that this implies the Earth exists as their world of origin, or at least a world similar to “our” Earth in many respects. Whether it's our Earth or merely a parallel one with similar nations,
whether it still exists or whether it was destroyed long ago - these matters are dark to us. Does “our” Earth exist in Dungeons & Dragons? Yes, it's appeared in a number of places. In “The City Beyond the Gate” in Dragon #100, characters from a D&D world must venture to London, England in 1983 to retrieve the Mace of Cuthbert from a museum. In The Immortal Storm, a party of godlike Immortals
have to travel to New York and Chicago in pursuit of the essence of smell. In Castle Greyhawk the PCs find a portal to Bombay, India circa 1945, and there's a whole sideplot where Mordenkainen travels to Hollywood (circa 1987) to make fantasy movies, casting the PCs in them. It is was the common thought of originators Dungeons & Dragons that the elves of many of the worlds came from Tolkien's Middle-earth when they left Middle-Earth. The Forgotten Realms and Hollow world had migrations of people from Egypt, Mesopotamia, ancient Greece and Rome, and pagan Ireland in its
history. These might well have been those actual nations from our 
Earth, though official materials leave this vague. Ed Greenwood wrote a series of articles in Dragon Magazine called “The Wizards Three,” which feature Elminster, Mordenkainen, and Dalamar (the elven wizard from Krynn) meeting
together at Ed Greenwood's house (with Ed Greenwood hidden in a suit of armor, taking notes), swapping spells and sampling Earth cuisine.
Occasionally other characters from Oerth or Toril have shown up as well. The conceit behind Ed Greenwood's Forgotten Realms articles has always been that
these have been dictated to him by Elminster himself, who uses his spell Elminster's Worldwalk and various portals to appear on Earth and chat with him about the Forgotten Realms. There is actually more than one Earth in D&D. In an ancient issue of Polyhedron, Gary Gygax spoke of the seven parallel worlds: Earth is the least magical and most technological of the five; Oerth is the most magical and least technological and Arda evolving away from magic to technology
during an age of man. Murlynd, a quasi-deity who was originally a PC in Gygax's home campaign, has been to Earth; in the adventure Dungeonland the PCs explore his house, which is equipped with such Earthly conveniences as a VCR. In the adventure Castle Amber, the PCs go to medieval France, but not the France of our world; they go to the parallel Earth of Clark Ashton
Smith, whose stories tie into Lovecraft's Mythos. In “Chronomancy and the Multiverse,” an article published on WotC's website (originally in TSR's AOL
site), Roger E. Moore says that this Earth is the same as the Gothic Earth described in the Masque of the Red Death setting, and the same as the various fantasy Earth cultures described in the Historical Reference series of accessories: The Celts, The Glory of Rome, Age of Heroes, Vikings, A
Mighty Fortress, Charlemagne's Paladins, The Crusades. There's also Midgard, a Prime world entirely dominated by Norse myths, where the serpent Jormungandr literally wraps itself around the ocean, described in Dragon Magazine #90 and the 0D&D Northern Reaches Gazetteer. The d20 Modern accessory Urban Arcana describes a version of Earth that has been secretly invaded by beings from the D&D worlds beyond the Plane of Shadow. One Planescape NPC exists there: the ogre mage Estavan, who's apparently found a portal from Earth to Sigil. So yes, Earth exists in D&D, and even if it hasn't been explicitly mentioned in anything that says “Planescape” on the cover, I think you can say it exists in Planescape as well. The question is, which Earth do you mean? A portal from Sigil could touch many alternate versions of the world: an ancient Earth where the gods of Olympus still rule, a modern Earth where no
one knows magic is real, and a modern Earth where elves, dwarves, (and orcs) have returned and are reintroducing magic to the masses, and a version of Earth where gods, vampires, and mages have always guided society in secret are just a few of the many possibilities.

Kesh has a strong fortified harbor, and maintains its own fleet to interdict pirates from the [[southern_archipelago|archipelago]] . krynn: Krynn Krynn is a city of the [[elflands|Elflands]] , ruled over by [[gilthanas|King Gilthanas Kanan of House Eventine]] , on the Northern shore of the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] . Krynn has a large [[dargonesti_elves|Dargonesti]] population,  and it is from this port that they usually hire out to shipping expeditions.  It has significant ship building and repair, as well as an underwater neighborhood in the [[dargonesti_sound|Dargonesti Sound]] .  Glassteel diving bells allow air breathing visitors, however it is a rare privilege to be granted. Grey pearls and a wide variety of seafood are harvested by the aquatic elves. Meanwhile, landward, Silvenesti and Qualinesti elves patrol the forests, build shipping, and provide services for the port.  Elven alcoholic flower nectar, magically extracted, is a popular beverage in the many inns and taverns, as are the excellent local meads. [[places_on_arda|Places on Arda Main Page]]
